articles.headline: Premier League live updates: Cole Palmer starts as Chelsea host Bournemouth
articles.description: After a three-week international break, club soccer returns! Chelsea will look to bounce back from their loss to Brentford last time out as they host Bournemouth.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ速報：チェルシー対ボーンマス、コール・パーマーが先発
articles.descriptionJa: 3週間の代表ウィークを終え、クラブサッカーが再開！チェルシーはホームでのボーンマス戦で、前回のブレントフォード戦の敗北から立ち直れるか。
articles.body:
After a three-week international break, European club soccer returns this weekend!

We kicked things off in the Premier League with defending champions Arsenal having to come from behind to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium.

Next up in England, Chelsea take on Bournemouth as part of a busy Saturday slate. Our match of the day then sees two teams desperate to turn their seasons around, as Manchester United host a Tottenham Hotspur side who are bottom of the table and still searching for its first league win of the season.

There's plenty of action across the continent, too. In LaLiga, Alavés face Atlético Madrid before champions Barcelona host Getafe. Bayern Munich take on Augsburg in the Bundesliga, and Inter Milan face Parma in Serie A.

Enjoy all the updates from Saturday's matches.

articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの最有望株JJガブリエルが、バイエルン・ミュンヘンとの交渉を再開。最新情報はTransfer Talkで。
articles.body:
Manchester United's top young prospect JJ Gabriel has renewed discussions with Bayern Munich, while Fulham's Josh King is a target for Liverpool/ Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich have held fresh talks with Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel's representatives over a potential move, Sky Germany reports. The Bundesliga giants have not made an offer to the 16-year-old because they have yet to receive a firm commitment from him, and they fear that he favours a move to Spain. A January switch is planned for Gabriel --  who has not trained with United since walking out on the club ahead of their Carabao Cup tie with Brighton & Hove AlbionBrighton & Hove on Sept. 16 -- but United want to retain the teenager.

- Liverpool are considering a January move for Fulham midfielder Josh King, according to Football Insider. The 19-year-old is also attracting interest from Arsenal, Manchester United, Borussia Dortmund and Barcelona after an impressive start to the season. Fulham are reluctant to lose him, but Liverpool view King as a potential long-term addition and will continue monitoring his performances before deciding whether to make a move. He is under contract at Craven Cottage until June 2029.

- Bayern Munich have renewed their interest in Barcelona midfielder Dani Olmo and could consider a January move, beIN Sports reports. The 28-year-old remains part of Hansi Flick's plans but faces competition from Fermín López for playing time. Barcelona could listen to offers in the region of €90 million, although no formal bid has been confirmed. Olmo is under contract until 2030, with several Premier League clubs also monitoring his situation.

- Nottingham Forest would require an exceptional offer to consider letting Murillo leave the club in January amid interest from Manchester United, TEAMtalk reports. The Brazilian centre-back is also admired by Liverpool and Chelsea, but Forest regard a midseason departure as highly unlikely. Murillo signed a new contract until 2030 back in May, strengthening the club's negotiating position.

- Real Madrid and Barcelona could tempt Michael Olise away from Bayern Munich, but the winger has little interest in returning to the Premier League, TEAMtalk reports. Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City remain keen admirers, although the France international is settled in Germany and is open to discussing a new contract. Bayern are prepared to offer a substantial pay rise, while both Spanish clubs have made their interest known to his representatives.

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim says Man United struggles prepared him for AC Milan challenge
articles.description: Ruben Amorim believes the ups and downs of his management career have prepared him well for the task of leading AC Milan.
articles.headlineJa: ルーベン・アモリム、マン・ユナイテッドでの苦難がACミランでの挑戦への備えになったと語る
articles.descriptionJa: ルーベン・アモリムは、自身の監督キャリアにおける浮き沈みが、ACミランを率いるという任務に向けて自身を十分に鍛えてくれたと考えている。
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim believes the ups and downs of his management career have prepared him well for the task of leading AC Milan.

Amorim enjoyed an excellent start to his time in the dugout at Sporting Lisbon before a demoralising stint at Manchester United that saw him sacked after 14 months.

Now in charge of the Rossoneri, who entered the international break fifth in Serie A and head to Sassuolo on Sunday, the 41-year-old feels content that he is the right man in the right place.

"The experience we've built up at other clubs helps us with every challenge, or new challenge," Amorim told DAZN.

"Here it's more similar to Portugal. It's a different kind of pressure, because people outside the club experience the team really passionately. I'm used to living like that.

"In England it's a bit different, obviously. Manchester United are a global club just like Milan, so every single thing you do carries weight, and that has helped me try to conduct myself in the best way here at Milan. In my head, everything I've experienced in my career was to reach this point, at this very special club, to be ready to help it."

Amorim will be hoping summer signing Gonçalo Ramos carries his international form into the clash at Mapei Stadium, with the Champions League winner netting in three out of Portugal's four Nations League games.

- Chelsea's Cole Palmer signs new contract until 2034

- Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola offers backing to Bradley Barcola

- Carrick: No timeline for Benjamin Sesko's Man United return

He has just one goal for Milan so far but has impressed with his tireless work-rate, a quality Amorim has no intention of curbing.

"I'm not going to say Ramos should run less. I'll never say that about a player," he said.

"The key thing is that we're scoring, and that's what matters most. I know full well that a striker needs to score goals, and he will score, but he's working hard, and if we're scoring, it's also thanks to Gonçalo Ramos."

articles.headline: Can the Seahawks' defense again silence the 49ers' hot offense Sunday?
articles.description: Seattle's defense stole the show the past two times these teams met. But the 49ers and Brock Purdy are on a roll heading into Week 5.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスの守備は、日曜日に再び好調な49ersの攻撃を封じ込められるか？
articles.descriptionJa: 前回までの2度の対戦では、シアトルの守備が主役となった。しかし、49ersとブロック・パーディは第5週に向けて勢いに乗っている。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- It took Mike Macdonald several weeks to rewatch the Seattle Seahawks' 29-13 victory in Super Bowl LX. It was partly because of his packed schedule and partly because of his perfectionist ways. The head coach and defensive playcaller knew that even though his unit had dominated the New England Patriots, it had also made miscues that would eat at him once he saw them on film.

Macdonald had no such hang-ups about either of Seattle's two January victories over the San Francisco 49ers, a pair of defensive masterpieces in which the Seahawks held their divisional rivals out of the end zone -- first in Week 18, then again in the divisional round of the playoffs.

That was then.

The 49ers (4-0) and their offense are rolling heading into an NFC West clash with the Seahawks (3-1) on Sunday at Lumen Field. San Francisco ranks second in points per game (30.5), Brock Purdy leads the league in Total QBR (89.2), and the quarterback has a few playmakers who weren't on the team nine months ago.

"None of what happened last year matters," Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV said. "It's a new year, new season. They've got a hell of a group. They've put together four good games, won every one of them. Just like we have a new team, they've got a new team. They're doing some different things. We've just got to go out there and do our job."

In the first of two defensive performances that even Macdonald might have considered perfect, the Seahawks held Kyle Shanahan's team to 173 total yards in last year's regular-season finale, a winner-take-all affair in which the NFC West and No. 1 seed were on the line. Seattle intercepted one of Purdy's passes, forced two more turnovers on downs and limited Christian McCaffrey to 23 yards on eight carries in a 13-3 victory at Levi's Stadium.

When the Seahawks hosted the 49ers after their first-round bye, it was more of the same. Macdonald's top-ranked scoring defense allowed only 236 yards, generated three takeaways to go along with three more turnovers on downs, and bottled up McCaffrey again (35 rushing yards on 11 attempts) in a 41-6 rout.

While appearing on NBC's pregame coverage of Super Bowl LX, Shanahan said self-deprecatingly that his "expert opinion" on the Seahawks might not be worth much given that his offense couldn't generate a touchdown against them during the past two times they met.

"We tackled really well. We limited extra yardage. I thought we rushed the quarterback with discipline and married the coverage," Macdonald recalled this week. "That's what it takes to play really good football, in general. But the guys played hard, played physical, played well situationally."

Said safety Julian Love: "I think we communicated really well. I think these guys do a lot of stuff pre-snap, motions, shifts, crazy alignment-type things. articles.headline: Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa start for Arsenal against Leeds despite picking up injuries on international duty
articles.description: Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa have been named in Arsenal's starting lineup for the visit of Leeds United despite withdrawing from their national team camps with injury in the recent Nations League window.
articles.headlineJa: カイ・ハフェルツとエズリ・コンサ、代表活動中の負傷にもかかわらずリーズ戦でアーセナルの先発に
articles.descriptionJa: カイ・ハフェルツとエズリ・コンサは、先日のネーションズリーグ期間中に負傷のため代表キャンプを離脱していたものの、ホームでリーズ・ユナイテッドを迎えるアーセナルの先発ラインナップに名を連ねた。
articles.body:
LONDON -- Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa have been named in Arsenal's starting lineup for the visit of Leeds United despite withdrawing from their national team camps with injury in the recent Nations League window.

Havertz went off after 30 minutes in Germany's first game of the international window against Netherlands, and subsequently returned to Arsenal for further treatment.

Konsa started England's games against Spain and Croatia but withdrew from the squad ahead of the home clash against Czechia.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had kept his cards close to his chest when discussing their fitness in his news conference on Friday.

"With Kai, he had a muscular injury, so I spoke to Jurgen [Klopp] and immediately they sent the player back, as is normal, " Arteta said.

"Ezri has been carrying some issues as well and we had good communication with the England camp about that."

- Arteta: Premier League still best in the world despite Man City verdict

- What's next for Man City: How long will appeals, punishments take?

- Premier League reranked: Have we found Arsenal's fatal flaw?

Havertz's fitness concerns were expected to open a spot in the starting lineup for Viktor Gyökeres, who scored four times for Sweden in the recent Nations League window.

However, the Swede has to again settle for a role on the bench as his wait for a first league start goes on.

Declan Rice also starts for Arsenal after sitting out England's recent spate of games, while Myles Lewis-Skelly also returns to the starting lineup after being restricted to a bench role in their previous league game against Brighton.

Noni Madueke has been deployed on the left wing ahead of Eberechi Eze, with Christos Tzolis sidelined with injury.

articles.headline: Chelsea's Cole Palmer signs new contract until 2034
articles.description: Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension keeping him at Chelsea until 2034.
articles.headlineJa: チェルシーのコール・パーマー、2034年までの新契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: コール・パーマーは契約延長に合意し、2034年までチェルシーに残留することとなった。
articles.body:
Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension keeping him at Chelsea until 2034.

The new deal extends the England forward's commitment by a year, with Palmer having signed for an extra two years until 2033 in August 2024.

The 24-year-old said on chelseafc.com: "Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I'm delighted to sign and I'm obviously very happy.

"Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence, so it was only right to sign.

"Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it, too."

Palmer excelled upon joining the Blues from Manchester City in August 2023 and has made 91 goal contributions in 138 appearances so far.

He struggled with a persistent groin problem last season and was rebuked by England head coach Thomas Tuchel after not making himself available for the recent internationals, with Chelsea keen to manage his load.

- Man City 'a disgrace; I would throw them out' - furious Ian Holloway

- Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

Palmer has started the season strongly, though, scoring four goals in seven appearances.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso insisted on Friday that Palmer, who missed out on the World Cup, is committed to England, saying: "He has to be fully fit to play.

"And, when he's fully fit, he will enjoy his minutes. We need him in that moment: the club and the national team."

This is the latest deal stretching into the 2030s given out by Chelsea and follows on from recent contracts signed by João Pedro and Pedro Neto.

articles.headline: NFL Week 5 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
articles.description: Big performances for Brock Bowers, Travon Walker and Luther Burden III? The Giants pulling an upset? And an under-the-radar RB emerging this week in fantasy?
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週の予測：番狂わせ、ファンタジーの伏兵、スタッツ、TDスコアラーなど
articles.descriptionJa: ブロック・バワーズ、トラボン・ウォーカー、ルーサー・バーデン3世が躍動するか？ジャイアンツが番狂わせを起こすか？そして今週、ファンタジーで注目を集める隠れたRBが登場するか？
articles.body:
Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Buccaneers defeated the Cowboys on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 14 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Giants pull off an upset? How many yards will Steelers running back Jaylen Warren record against the Colts? Is Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett a safe starter in fantasy? And which Bears receiver will find the end zone? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Las Vegas Raiders +3.5 (+164 moneyline) at New England Patriots

Patriots QB Drake Maye's breakout against the Bills last week didn't solve New England's protection problems. He was still heavily pressured, while his receivers didn't create much yardage after the catch.

Meanwhile, Raiders QB Kirk Cousins has a useful answer against this defense: play-action. New England is much tougher when quarterbacks simply drop back, but it has allowed the fifth-highest QBR against play-action this season. That fits what Cousins does best, giving Las Vegas a way to manufacture enough offense to create tension.

New York Giants +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Washington Commanders

Giants QB Jameis Winston showed against the Cardinals last week that he can find WR Malik Nabers and produce touchdowns. That ability, combined with the Commanders' poor pass defense, is what makes this a live play Sunday. Washington's blitz-happy approach only helps if it disrupts Winston before he finds those openings.

Offensively, the Commanders will return QB Jayden Daniels, but they've struggled to stay out of third-and-long. The Giants' secondary has limited passing yardage while creating interceptions this season (six, tied for the most in the NFL).

Walder predicts three stat lines

Jaylen Warren, RB, Pittsburgh Steelers: 16 carries, 104 yards, 1 touchdown, 1 reception, 19 receiving yards

Warren has been getting a heavy workload this season, and there's no reason that shouldn't continue Sunday against the Colts. Indy ranks 30th in run stop win rate and 25th in opponent EPA per designed carry. It has surrendered 4.8 yards per carry (tied for fifth most), and that number holds steady against duo runs, which the Steelers run frequently (33% of the time).

I do expect Warren's production will be more on the ground in this game than usual, however, because the Colts play a lot of man coverage, which usually discourages RB targets and receptions.

articles.headline: Can Burrow, Bengals establish identity vs. Dolphins?
articles.description: The Bengals put Burrow under center but ultimately went back to what the QB knows best. What's next?
articles.headlineJa: バーロウとベンガルズは、ドルフィンズ戦でチームのアイデンティティを確立できるか？
articles.descriptionJa: ベンガルズはバーロウをセンターに据えたものの、最終的にはQBが最も得意とする形に戻った。次の一手はどうなるのか？
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- When the Cincinnati Bengals needed to make something happen, quarterback Joe Burrow and the offense relied on what they knew best.

Over the past several months, Cincinnati took a slew of reps with Burrow lined up under center, an indication that Cincinnati wanted to expand the menu of options available to the former MVP finalist.

But ultimately, Burrow and Cincinnati went into shotgun.

Through four games, the Bengals are still trying to figure out the best way to operate offensively. And it puts the mission for this Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins (0-4) squarely into focus as the Bengals try to find what parts of the offense fit.

"We have to improve at them -- we can't just abandon them -- and find what our identity is going to be these last three quarters of the season," offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said Monday.

What the Bengals are doing under center falls squarely into that category. Entering Sunday, Cincinnati is last in the NFL in yards per play while under center (3.3). And after an offseason of trying to put Burrow beneath center Ted Karras, the Bengals lead the NFL in shotgun usage (72.3%).

Those numbers are heavily skewed because of what happened in the team's recent outing. The Bengals had 15 carries for just 23 yards. According to ESPN Research, that was Cincinnati's lowest total since the 2012 season.

And with that not working, Cincinnati leaned on throwing the ball. Burrow had the fourth-most dropbacks in his career (58) and the Bengals were in shotgun formation on 85.5% of the team's snaps.

After the 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday after 2-0 start, Burrow talked about throwing the ball even more when the run game is struggling.

A few days later -- and after he had some time to cool off -- a more sensible approach prevailed.

"We have to be more balanced going forward, and a big part of that is the run game," Burrow said.

And Cincinnati's ever-confident and contact-embracing quarterback also espoused his belief that the team shouldn't abandon its vision of an offense that can operate effectively from under center.

"We obviously have to be better at it," Burrow said. "We're still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it's very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to be better."

Getting better in one specific area is crucial. As Burrow explained, being able to use play-action passes from under center requires having a run game that defenses actually respect. Otherwise, a team's offensive linemen will be subjected to edge rushers who didn't buy the fake and are screaming toward the quarterback.

"That's not a recipe for success," Burrow said.

The Bengals have worked at trying to build a more explosive rushing attack. In the weeks leading up to the Jacksonville loss, Cincinnati coach Zac Taylor talked about the team being close to finding big runs that can make things easier on the offense.

articles.headline: How wild-card game sent Bears, Packers in opposite directions
articles.description: Ever since Chicago sent Green Bay home, the Bears have taken flight and the Packers can't find their footing.
articles.headlineJa: ワイルドカード戦が、いかにしてベアーズとパッカーズを正反対の運命へと導いたか
articles.descriptionJa: シカゴがグリーンベイを敗退させて以来、ベアーズは勢いに乗っている一方で、パッカーズは足場を固められずにいる。
articles.body:
Nearly nine months later, two things remain true about the Jan. 10, 2026, wild-card playoff game between the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field: It was an epic event on its own, but it also deeply affected the course of each franchise and the vibe around each team.

While the Bears were eliminated from the playoffs a week later in an overtime loss to the Los Angeles Rams, confidence has gushed from Chicago ever since quarterback Caleb Williams capped an improbable comeback and a 25-point fourth-quarter barrage with the game-winning touchdown to DJ Moore to eliminate the Packers from the playoffs 31-27, thus ending their season on a five-game losing streak.

That game, combined with another improbable comeback against the Packers less than a month earlier, validated everything that coach Ben Johnson preached when he got the job about his team's approach to their rivals from up North.

From Johnson's comment during his introductory news conference -- when he said how much he enjoyed beating LaFleur twice a year when he was the Detroit Lions' offensive coordinator -- to his "F--- the Packers" exclamation in the locker room after the playoff game, the Bears coach hasn't been shy about injecting himself into the rivalry.

Everyone in the Bears' locker room after Sunday's 23-12 win over the New York Jets had to know what was coming from Johnson at some point during his postgame speech. He saved it for the end.

"You guys know what next week is?" Johnson exclaimed.

"You guys know what next week is?" he repeated for emphasis. "Enough said."

Meanwhile in Green Bay, the blown 21-3 lead in the playoff game hung over coach Matt LaFleur -- and all the high-ranking decision-makers in the Packers organization for that matter -- like the sword of Damocles. Just like in ancient Greek story, the sword has seemingly followed them ever since, just waiting to drop.

As much as Johnson has enjoyed poking the Packers since he got the job, LaFleur has taken a different approach, which he reiterated this week.

"This game is about players, and so we'll keep it about the players," LaFleur said. "I'm not the one out there playing, so I think that's always been my mentality, and we're going to keep it about those guys.

 "And don't get me wrong, I love the rivalry. It's awesome. It's great. It's intense. You can feel it on game day. You can feel it throughout the course of the week, and also the significance. I mean, they're the defending North champions. So, what a great opportunity, great challenge for us in our home stadium to play against the defending champs."

The two teams meet again Sunday at Lambeau Field (1:00 p.m. ET, Fox) for the 214th time, playoffs included, in their storied histories. While only one game separates the Bears (3-1) and the Packers (2-2) in the NFC North standings, they look like organizations that have headed in opposite directions since the last meeting.

articles.headline: Texans, Titans face off desperately seeking first win after 0-4 starts
articles.description: Tennessee coach Robert Saleh and Houston coach DeMeco Ryans put friendship aside in battle of winless teams.
articles.body:
For the second consecutive year, the Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans will face off in desperate need of their first win of the season.

Last season was a matchup between two 0-3 teams, only for this year to be even more dire with both sitting at 0-4 for their meeting in Nashville, Tennessee, on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

Houston won last year's matchup 23-0 en route to a 12-5 record and a trip to the divisional round of the playoffs. Meanwhile, the Titans finished 3-14 for the second straight season and earned the No. 4 pick in the draft.

The Titans currently have a 10-game losing streak to AFC South opponents and are tied for the current longest regular-season losing streak at six games, and Houston, a team that came in with Super Bowl aspirations and were considered favorites to win the AFC South, needs to defy the odds (only one team -- the 1992 Chargers -- have made the playoffs after starting 0-4) to make the postseason for a fourth straight season.

"Anything's achievable." Titans coach Robert Saleh said Wednesday, "You get on a run and you start getting -- like momentum and confidence is such a big deal and a very, very underrated thing in the NFL. I just feel like if we can just get one, it'll snowball and who knows what will happen. But it's never over until that little 'E' shows up on the standings ... or whatever signifies that you've been eliminated. You just keep on fighting and even when you are eliminated, it still doesn't matter. You still got to show up and do your best."

For now, both are looking up at the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) and Indianapolis Colts (2-2) in the division through four weeks.

"One of the things we talk about is owning the South," Saleh said. "Owning it is not just a one-time thing. We want to own it for as long as we're here and this is our first crack at a division opponent."

The Texans already fell to the Colts in Week 3 in the only interdivisional game amongst AFC South teams in the first four weeks, so they already sit at the bottom of the division in that regard as well.

But if Houston were to get its first win of the season, Ryans would not only be denying one of his closest friends from getting his first win this season, he'd also be denying him from getting his first win as the head coach of the Titans.

"Saleh means a lot to me and when it comes to coaching and why I'm coaching," Ryans said. "He's going to have his guys fired up, ready to play. We're in the same position. I know he's bringing his best, we have to bring our best. It's always going to be a great matchup. He knows what we do. We have to know what he does defensively. May the best man win."

Titans looking to change directions

At this point, it looks like desperation is peaking for the Titans. Saleh said the team has to learn how not to lose before it can learn how to win. He pointed to turnovers, penalties and missed assignments as weekly examples of how the team puts itself behind the 8-ball.

articles.body:
Each week during the 2026 NFL season, these fantasy football IDP rankings will be updated by fantasy analysts Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.

We've split up our fantasy football rankings by traditional IDP (individual defensive players) positions: defensive line, linebacker and defensive back. Scoring systems can vary greatly in IDP formats, so these rankings are based on the following scoring criteria:

Solo tackle: 1.5 points

Assisted tackle: 0.75 points

Tackle for loss: 2 points

Sack: 4 points

Interception: 5 points

Forced fumble: 4 points

Fumble recovery: 4 points

Defensive TD: 6 points

Safety: 2 points

Pass defensed: 1.5 points

articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーバスケットボール・チートシート：ドラフトに欠かせない重要プレイヤー名一覧
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-27シーズンのファンタジーバスケットボール・ドラフトガイドから、印刷可能なPDF形式のチートシートに知っておくべき全プレイヤー名をまとめました。
articles.body:
The 2026-27 fantasy basketball season is just around the corner and drafts are happening right now! Are you prepared? We bet you are. But if you're not, we also bet we can get you there.

Either way, you need the Fantasy Basketball Cheat Sheet. How does it differ from other cheat sheets? Well, these aren't rankings, (although we have those too). Rather, we've aggregated all the names you need to know from the best preseason content we've put out over the past month-plus.

So you can read André Snellings' Ultimate Draft Board or Eric Karabell's Do and Do Not Draft lists and get an edge over the competition on draft day.

This cheat sheet covers the names you need to know from:

André Snellings' Ultimate Draft Board

Eric Karabell's 'Do Not Draft' List

Karabell's 'Do Draft' List

Staff's sleepers, breakouts and busts

From rankings and projections to sleepers, breakouts and busts, we've got you covered from every angle, all in one convenient place.

Create, reactivate or join a league today!

Top 150 H2H roto and category rankings 

Snellings reveals his top 150 players for leagues that use roto and category scoring systems.

Sortable player projections

Every point, rebound, steal, 3-pointer, block, turnover, steal, field goal and free throw taken makes a difference in fantasy. We have them all projected for you right here.
